definition: Concise means brief and direct in expression — saying everything that needs saying in the fewest words that will do it.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word concise. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know concise should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: Editors loved her concise match reports: ninety minutes of soccer delivered in six tight sentences.
Economical wording is milder than concise: it trims obvious excess but keeps its comfortable phrases, while concise writing pares everything down to the words that earn their place.
Curt goes further than concise: concise trims a message to its essentials and stays polite, while a curt reply is cut so short it borders on rude.

Succinct means compactly and neatly complete — nearly a twin of concise. Succinct leans toward praise for the elegance of the compression; concise is the plainer, matter-of-fact word for saying it in few words.
Terse means stripped so bare it can read as cold or curt — terse brevity has an edge to it. Concise brevity stays civil: nothing extra, but nothing chilly either.
Pithy means brief and loaded — a pithy line carries wit or wisdom concentrated into a phrase. Concise promises only economy; a grocery list can be concise, but it takes a proverb to be pithy.

It measures length against need — which is why it differs from this unit's lucid, a claim about clarity rather than brevity: a concise note can still confuse, and a lucid lecture can fill an afternoon.
Push brevity past politeness and you land on terse or curt; keep the essentials and you stay concise.
Teachers asking for 'a concise answer' are asking you to cut, not to omit.

The new park ranger inherited a trail guide that ran to sixty pages, and watched hikers leave it in the rack.
Over the winter she rewrote it into a single laminated card.
Every trail kept its distance, its climb, and its one real hazard; everything else went.
Rangers began calling the card the most concise document the park had ever printed, and hikers finally carried it.
Nothing a walker needed was missing, her supervisor noted — it had simply stopped hiding behind words a walker didn't.
